paragraphs: Guardian Alliance Technologies sells background investigation software built for law enforcement agencies, fire departments and other public safety agencies. The company describes it as an end-to-end background investigation solution that gives agencies a way to pre-screen, investigate and approve applicants. It is sold on monthly and annual plans. The site says over 1,500 agencies nationwide use it.

The process starts with a quick assessment of each applicant to decide whether a full investigation should be conducted. From there, a centralized data center stores an applicant's job-seeking activity, such as the agencies they have applied to. That record gives investigators access to all applicant answers provided to any agency in the Guardian Alliance. Access to the National Decertification Index is a free, standard part of the Triage Center, which the company says helps agencies identify decertified applicants.

Guardian states that it complies with the FBI CJIS Security Policy. President and founder Justin Biedinger describes ten years on patrol and 3 years as a background investigator before the tools were built. He says the tools mimic existing background processes while giving investigators more efficient means to do their job. A June 2022 news item announces the addition of more than 80 new law enforcement agencies since the start of that year.
